advances: This is a conditional raw positive-width exclusion in one integer variable. It supplies no cap-union volume estimate and makes no assertion that facet contact gives the needed volume gap.

proof:
Fix a mark $y_1\in K_1$ and put $w=h\Gamma(\ell)$. On $K_1$ take the two through-mark opposite margins $s=\ell(x-y_1)$ and $-s$. Their outward ramps satisfy
$$
\varphi_w(s)+\varphi_w(-s)\le 1+\mathbf1_{\{|s|\le w\}}.
$$
Since $K_1\subset K$, its slab volume in $|s|\le w$ is at most $2w C_\ell$. The sum of the two own smoothed masses is therefore at most $|K_1|+2w C_\ell$, and one is at most $|B|/2+h G_\ell C_\ell$.

Either own cap can be realized at the same mass in the actual mixed set: add $A(z-1)$ to its signed continuous margin, with $A>0$ sufficiently large. Every other sampled base has $z-1\le-1$. Compactness bounds the continuous evaluations, so a finite $A$ makes every outside margin at most $-w$. The target-fiber margin and width are unchanged. Taking the infimum over mixed caps proves the upper bound.

Let $y_0$ be the ordinary centroid of $K$. The full-volume metronoid in 6769574fc1bd9f8d consists of this centroid, so every own closed halfspace through $y_0$ has mass at least $\gamma_d|K|$. Every mixed through-mark cap at $(0,y_0)$ contributes at least this much on $K$ because the outward ramp is one on its ordinary closed trace. A pure-base cap through $0$ contributes the whole own mass. Thus $(0,y_0)$ has depth at least $\gamma_d|K|$, which proves the exclusion under the strict comparison. Under the complete-miss and strict support-gap hypotheses of b5d53d637e045f65, that result supplies $K_1\subset K_{\mathcal B}\subset K$ and rules out every sampled base at least two. The small-width consequence follows by choosing $hG_\ell C_\ell$ smaller than the fixed half-volume gap.
statement: Let $C\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact and convex. Suppose its positive-volume fibers $K=K_0$ and $K_1$ satisfy $K_1\subset B\subset K$ for a measurable $B$, and there is no nonempty fiber at any integer $z\ge2$. Use raw uniform outward-smoothed mixed depth with widths $h\Gamma(u)$ for a fixed covariance norm $\Gamma$, and ordinary closed pure-base caps. For any fixed nonzero continuous functional $\ell$, let $C_\ell$ bound the density of $\ell_*(\mathbf1_K\,dx)$ and let $G_\ell\ge\Gamma(\ell)$. Every point of $K_1$ has depth at most $|B|/2+hG_\ell C_\ell$. If this is less than $\gamma_d|K|$, where $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, base $1$ has no deepest mark. In the setting of the reflected support-gap certificate b5d53d637e045f65, its complete-miss hypotheses and strict support gap supply containment and exposure for $B=K_{\mathcal B}$. A fixed gap $|K_{\mathcal B}|<2\gamma_d|K|$ suffices for small $h$ when $G_\ell C_\ell$ is bounded independently of $h$.
title: Finite-width depth test for an exposed fiber
